expectations.text: Output is a numbered list (not unstructured bullets or prose paragraphs)
expectations.evidence: Output uses numbered items #1 through #8 with clear categories

expectations.text: Output references specific rules from the actual CLAUDE.md content (e.g. dd-git, RTK, testing rules, writing rules) rather than giving generic advice
expectations.evidence: Explicitly references dd-git-normalize.sh, pr-draft-enforce.sh, rtk-rewrite.sh, justins-voice-detect.sh by name

expectations.text: Output categorizes findings using terms like stale, redundant, wrong layer, or well-placed
expectations.evidence: Uses explicit categories: Bugs/correctness, Redundancy, Stale content, Logic gap, Well-placed but unused

expectations.text: Output does not auto-apply changes — asks for approval before modifying any files
expectations.evidence: Ends with: 'Want me to apply all of these, or go through them one at a time?'

expectations.text: Output references hooks or settings.json as a better enforcement layer for at least one rule
expectations.evidence: Multiple references to hook layer, specifically flags that justins-voice-detect.sh has stdin bug and dd-git-normalize.sh blanket-approves destructive operations
